mechanism.summary: The captured page advertises an urgent 'Personal Assistant / Payment Agent' job at $650/week on a jewelry-gallery domain, promising weekly 'duty funds' so the worker never uses personal money, and the Caldera application form harvests identity data (full name, date of birth, mailing address, cell phone) plus bank information ('Owns a Bank Account?', 'Bank Name ... Our Payroll Platform'). The synthetic condition (Payment Agent terms): the duty funds are deposited into the agent's personal bank account and the balance must be forwarded to company suppliers within 24 hours, with a $120 registration surety deducted from the first week funds and refunded only at week four.
mechanism.source_basis: FTC 'Job Scams' (fake check: 'Never bank on a...'; catalog C23 'Fake employer check and onward transfer'): employment scams that pay with a check and have the new hire forward money on from their own account (money mule).

blocks.text: Duty funds are provided by the company; you never use your own personal money for any task.

Q: How do the weekly duty funds work? A: Client payments for materials are deposited straight into your personal bank account every Monday. You deduct your $650 salary and forward the balance to company suppliers within 24 hours of receipt.

Q: Why do you need my bank name? A: Your bank must be on our Payroll Platform before duty funds can be dispatched to your account. If it is not listed, our HR desk calls you to complete manual enrollment by phone.

Q: Does it cost anything to start? A: A one-time $120 registration surety is deducted from your first week funds and refunded with your fourth weekly payment. Agents who leave before week four forfeit the surety.
